name: MessageShield AI
summary: An OCR-assisted message analysis app with a trained classifier, authenticated history and model monitoring.
problem: People receive suspicious messages as text and screenshots. I built a workflow that extracts the message, runs classification and risk analysis, and keeps a private analysis history.
caption: Live MessageShield account creation screen. Analysis and history require authentication.
built: Designed and developed the Flutter/Dart frontend, Python/FastAPI backend and PostgreSQL storage end to end.
Added camera/gallery OCR with Google ML Kit, message analysis endpoints, risk signals and per-user history.
Trained a TF-IDF and Logistic Regression classifier on 800 curated messages; evaluated on a stratified 200-message held-out split.
Implemented Firebase/JWT authentication, role-based authorization, ownership checks and sensitive-pattern redaction.
Added MLflow experiment/model tracking, inference-version monitoring, PSI category drift checks and backend/Flutter CI.
decision: I used an interpretable classical ML baseline and kept preprocessing and inference together. Model version tracking and category drift checks make changes to predictions easier to investigate.
evaluation: The classifier achieved 89.5% accuracy (179/200) and 89.2% weighted F1 on the held-out split of a 1,000-message curated dataset. These are classifier evaluation results, not a production scam-detection guarantee. Multilingual and real-world evaluation remain areas for improvement.
next: Expand language and edge-case coverage, strengthen the evaluation dataset, and compare multilingual embedding models against the existing baseline.

name: LegalLens AI
summary: Document-grounded legal research with hybrid retrieval, reranking, source citations and access-controlled workspaces.
problem: A useful document assistant needs to retrieve the right clauses and show where an answer came from. I built a research application that connects document processing, retrieval and cited responses.
caption: Document summary screen preview using sample data. Shown as a UI preview, not a benchmark result.
built: Designed and developed the Flutter/Dart frontend, FastAPI backend and PostgreSQL/pgvector database end to end.
Implemented PDF upload, extraction/OCR, chunking and 384-dimensional SentenceTransformer embeddings.
Combined semantic and BM25 retrieval with multi-query expansion, reciprocal rank fusion and cross-encoder reranking.
Added Groq-generated answers with source citations, saved conversations, document comparison and user, legal-professional and administrator workspaces.
Implemented Firebase authentication, owner-scoped access and duplicate detection, Cloudflare R2 document storage, and role/access tests.
decision: I combined keyword and semantic retrieval because a legal query can depend on both exact terms and meaning. Reranking and context selection sit before generation, while ownership checks constrain which documents a user can access.
evaluation: The project includes access-control and retrieval-related tests. I have not published a comprehensive legal-answer accuracy benchmark. Answers are research assistance and should be checked against the cited source documents.
next: Build a representative retrieval evaluation set, measure citation support, and expand checks for ambiguous or unsupported questions.

name: AI Travel Planner
summary: Discover places and turn travel preferences into validated, reviewable day-wise itinerary drafts.
problem: AI-generated itineraries need a reliable path from a draft to a saved trip. I built place discovery, planning and persistence with explicit validation and review before saving.
caption: Application home screen showing destination discovery and the trip-planning entry point.
built: Designed and developed the Flutter/Dart client, Python/FastAPI services and PostgreSQL database end to end, using SQLAlchemy for persistence.
Built destination/place discovery, saved places, trips and day-wise itineraries.
Integrated AI drafts from sourced places, structured output validation and user review before saving.
Enforced ownership, atomic trip saves and idempotency to avoid partial or duplicate records.
Implemented quota-aware Gemini/Groq routing, provider cooldowns, usage records, bounded discovery caching and source attribution.
Added coordinated token refresh in Dio, timeouts and one retry; configured Vercel web/Render API deployment and backend/Flutter CI.
decision: I treated AI output as a draft. Validation and review separate generation from persistence, and an idempotent save path protects against duplicate submissions. Provider cooldowns and usage tracking make quota failures easier to handle.
evaluation: Focused backend and Flutter checks cover selected application flows. Broader itinerary-quality and real-user evaluation remains to be completed. Hosted demo services may need time to initialize.
next: Expand device-level regression coverage and evaluate itinerary quality against a defined set of travel scenarios.
